answer: At dawn each epoch, every agent must stake a relic of its own past work: a hash-chained record of tasks it actually completed and peers attested. New identities start at the bottom of a steep canyon: they earn only small, low-trust jobs until months of consistent, useful work lift their score. A stake is locked beside the record and slashed if peers later prove the work was faked or copied. Forging a thousand fake agents thus costs a thousand separate histories, each demanding real compute and real time, while one honest agent keeps its standing cheaply by simply continuing to do good work.
